channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: [7] A van der Waals photon-ratchet for enhancing spin-defect emission and quantum sensing
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: O. V. Yazyev, A. Radenovic

Authors: E. Mayner, Y. Zhumagulov, C. de Giorgio, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Van der Waals heterostructure study on spin-defect emission for quantum sensing.

Tags: #vanderWaals #quantumsensing #heterostructure #hBN

Abstract: The weak photoluminescence of spin defects in hexagonal boron nitride limits their use in quantum technologies. Here, the authors demonstrate that a van der Waals heterostructure enhances defect emission by up to 45-fold at 4 K through interlayer optical coupling, with evidence supporting nonlinear photon-mediated excitation and interlayer energy-transfer pathways, while preserving magnetic-field readout and room-temperature operation.
